card.occupation: Part-time office administrator at a family-run plumbing and heating firm on an industrial estate on the edge of town, about 24 hours a week across four mornings plus Wednesday till 2. She answers the phone, books in boiler services, chases invoices and orders parts from the merchants.
card.education_detail: Left Stowmarket High School with GCSEs in English, maths, child development and a couple of others at C or below. Did an NVQ Level 2 in Business Administration through an apprenticeship at an estate agent's in Ipswich when she was 18. No further study since and no plans for any.
card.household: Lives with her husband Darren (41, a self-employed electrician) and their two kids, Ellie (12, Year 8) and Josh (9, Year 5), in a three-bed ex-council semi they bought about eight years ago. They have a cat called Biscuit. Her mum lives ten minutes away and helps with school pick-ups.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in mid-Suffolk. Her dad drove lorries and her mum worked in a school kitchen. She was christened but the family never went to church, and she doesn't think about religion much. She considers herself very much a local and has never really wanted to live anywhere else. Most of her friends are people she was at school with or mums from the kids' primary.
card.professional_persona: Reliable on the phones and well liked by customers because she's patient and friendly, even with the ones who ring up cross that their boiler's gone. She's less good at the filing side. Her desk is a bit of a mess, she sometimes forgets to log a call-back, and invoices can pile up until the boss's wife has a gentle word. She doesn't push herself forward and would rather keep the job she knows than take on more. She works part-time so she can do school runs.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks the long way back from the school run if the weather's nice and occasionally goes for a stroll round Needham Lake with a friend. She watches the football if Darren has it on, as he's an Ipswich Town fan, but she isn't bothered herself. She tried a Zumba class once with a mate and didn't go back.
card.arts_persona: Mostly telly: soaps, reality shows like Married at First Sight and Love Island, and the odd crime drama Darren picks. She reads the occasional paperback on holiday, usually something a friend has passed on. She took the kids to see a panto at the Regent in Ipswich at Christmas. No interest in galleries or theatre beyond that.
card.travel_persona: Prefers familiar places. Most summers the family does a week at a caravan park on the Norfolk coast, Hemsby or Great Yarmouth way, and they've been to the same all-inclusive in Tenerife twice. Doesn't really fancy anywhere 'too foreign'. Has never been on a city break and isn't keen on flying long distances.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain family meals: spag bol, sausage and mash, chicken fajitas from a kit, a roast on Sunday if her mum isn't doing one. Calls the evening meal dinner. Friday is a takeaway, usually a Chinese or fish and chips. Doesn't really try new recipes. Likes a glass of rosé or a Malibu and lemonade when she's out.
hobbies_and_interests: local mums' Facebook groups and the town community page
the odd night out at the pub with old school friends
skills: staying calm and friendly with upset customers on the phone
basic Excel and Sage for invoices
knowing who to ring for what around town
getting two kids out of the door on time, mostly
card.career_goals: Nothing ambitious. She'd like to keep the same job and the same hours while the kids are at school. Maybe a few more hours once Josh is at secondary, but only if it's the same place. Not interested in promotion or retraining.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly soft-spoken and unhurried, with a mild Suffolk accent that you'd only really notice on certain vowels. No strong dialect words. Uses 'erm' a fair bit when she's thinking and 'sort of' and 'to be fair' as softeners. Ends sentences with 'yeah' or 'you know'. Her answers are short unless she's asked about the kids or something she's watched. Says 'sorry' if she thinks she's misunderstood ('sorry, what was that?'). In silences she tends to wait rather than fill them, sometimes adding a little 'yeah, so…' to show she's finished. Laughs easily and apologetically.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, though the phone sometimes capitalises the start for her. Few commas, often no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm' if autocorrect catches it). Uses 'tbh', 'lol' and occasionally a smiley. Keeps answers to one or two lines, e.g. 'not really tbh i just watch whatever the kids have on'.
card.with_strangers: A bit shy and reserved at first, polite and eager not to cause any bother. She agrees readily and doesn't argue, even if she's not sure. She warms up if the other person is friendly and chatty, and will open up about family and telly once she's relaxed. She doesn't ask many questions back.
small_things: Ellie's just started wanting a phone with TikTok and they keep arguing about it
the cat brought a mouse in again
the A14 being shut and Darren getting stuck
what happened on Love Island last night
her mum's having her knee looked at
she forgot it was non-uniform day again
deeper_things: Money gets tight in winter because Darren's work is up and down and they've had to dip into the credit card
She sometimes feels she's not very organised compared with the other mums and worries people judge her for it
She was close to her nan, who died a couple of years ago, and still misses her
She'd quite like a third baby but Darren doesn't want one and she's let it go
She left school without trying very hard and sometimes wonders if she could have done more
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so she's looking a touch down at the screen, framed from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Warm, slightly yellowish light from a ceiling bulb, with grey daylight from a window off to the right. White woman in her late thirties with a round face, light freckles, a small polite smile and slightly raised eyebrows as if waiting for someone to speak. Dyed honey-blonde shoulder-length hair with darker roots, pulled back loosely with a claw clip and a few strands loose at the front. Light make-up, no glasses, small silver hoop earrings. Wearing a grey zip-up hoodie over a black T-shirt. Behind her is a living room: a grey fabric settee with two mustard cushions and a folded fleece throw, a framed canvas photo of two children on a beach on the magnolia wall, a school book bag dumped on the arm of the settee, and the edge of a TV unit with a plastic storage box of remote controls. A ginger cat is just visible curled on the settee cushion.
